subject: RFI: Endpoint fallback & surge resilience - requested benchmarking artefacts
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha@enterprize.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: James Liu <james.liu@enterprize.io>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: Endpoint fallback and surge resilience test requests

Hi Ben,

Thanks for taking this RFI. As part of our procurement evaluation we need a focused set of artifacts that describe how Redwood validates endpoint durability and graceful degradation under surge/burst conditions. Specifically, could you provide the following: 

- A short description of your test methodology for: steady-state throughput, burst soak, and cold-start recovery.
- Expected metrics at these phases (p50/p95/p99/p999 latency for token generation, tokens/sec, GPU utilization).
- How cache (prefix/KV) warm-up is handled and how it affects latency distributions.
- Typical concurrency per GPU and how you map requests to replicas during surges.
- Example traffic mixes (prompt lengths, streaming vs non-streaming) used in tests.
- Test artifacts: load scripts, metrics dashboards (or their schemas), and the runbook used to escalate/rollback if SLOs are violated.

We’d like these items by EOD Thursday (2026-11-05) to feed into our scoring. Happy to sign an NDA if you need to include any internal artifacts.

Best,
Asha Patel
Procurement Lead, Enterprize Inc.
asha@enterprize.io

Attachments: none
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@enterprize.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Endpoint fallback and surge resilience test requests

Hi Asha,

Thanks — we can provide a concise package and the artifacts you asked for. Attached is a starter workbook (rfi_benchmark_template.xlsx) and a short runbook (redwood-runbook.pdf). Below is a high-level overview; Marissa (perf eng) and Karthik (serving infra) are looped in for technical detail and test artifacts.

Summary of proposed approach (short):

1) Test phases
   - Baseline single-replica throughput: run steady QPS until throughput plateaus to characterize per-rep token/sec and latency envelope.
   - Concurrency scaling sweep: increase concurrent clients to observe p50/p95/p99/p999 latency inflection points and replica autoscaling triggers.
   - Burst soak + graceful degradation: inject short high-rate bursts (10x baseline) with varying inter-burst intervals to measure tail inflation and degradation modes (queueing, shedding, fallback to smaller model).
   - Cold-start injection: schedule controlled instance drain/recreation to measure cold-start added latency and warm-up curves for KV/prefix cache.

2) Key metrics collected
   - Per-request: p50/p95/p99/p999 generation latency (ms), time-to-first-token (ms) for streaming, tokens generated, request size (input tokens).
   - Infra: GPU utilization, memory pressure, kv-cache hit ratio, per-rep QPS, queue depth, error rates (4xx/5xx), tail-percentile CPU steal.
   - Business: cost-per-token approximation under each mode.

3) Cache & warm-up
   - We run two variants: cold (empty KV/prefix cache) and warm (synthetic warm-up crawl using representative prompt corpus). We report delta-latency and hit-rate growth. For production-like runs we recommend a 24–72 hour warm-up pass for large prefix caches.

4) Mapping & fallback behaviour
   - Requests are routed by policy: latency-sensitive preferring low-utilization replicas; cost-tiered routes can use quantized variants. When capacity saturates, automatic fallback can: (a) spill to dedicated lower-cost replica, (b) serve with quantized model with quality flag, or (c) fail fast depending on client policy — we’ll provide a matrix.

Proposed delivery
- Deliverables: completed workbook, JSON schema of metrics, sample load scripts (k6 + custom runner), Grafana dashboard snapshots, and a short runbook.
- Timeline: we can assemble the package and run the baseline tests within 48 hours; a complete sweep (including burst soak and cold-start runs) needs ~72 hours of lab time.

Next steps
- Let us know if we can proceed with the full sweep. If you prefer, we can run a short baseline and give preliminary numbers first.

Ben Carter
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: rfi_benchmark_template.xlsx, redwood-runbook.pdf
From: Asha Patel <asha@enterprize.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: James Liu <james.liu@enterprize.io>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:44:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Endpoint fallback and surge resilience test requests

Ben — thanks for the quick reply and the overview. A couple of clarifying questions before you run full sweeps: 

- For the burst soak, can you share how you generate request diversity? Do you use a seeded prompt corpus or synthetic templates? We care about prompt entropy because it affects KV patterns.
- When you refer to fallback to a quantized model, what quantization levels are you testing (e.g., 4-bit, 8-bit), and do you measure semantic drift (BLEU/ROUGE or embedding cosine) as part of degradation?
- For cold-starts, do you measure both container start time and model-mapping time (weights load + kernel compilation), and can you break down the components?

We are on a tight procurement timeline; a baseline within 48 hours is preferred — then we’ll see whether to proceed to full sweep. Also — please confirm if the runbook contains escalation contact info and live rollback commands (we may redact those under NDA).

Regards,
Asha

P.S. We will likely need the HubSpot deal link for approvals — I’ve included the ID in the worksheet request.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@enterprize.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 14:33:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Endpoint fallback and surge resilience test requests

Hi Asha —

Appreciate the specific asks. Quick answers and what we will include in the artefacts: 

- Burst request diversity: we use a mixed approach. For representative runs we seed with a corpus (anonymized customer prompts) that preserves token-length and entity distribution; for adversarial runs we use synthetic templates to maximize new KV keys. We’ll include the prompt corpus hash and a small sample set (anonymized) for reproducibility.

- Quantization & semantic drift: we test 8-bit and 4-bit quantized variants where supported. For degradation monitoring we compute embedding-cosine similarity and a small set of downstream metrics (classification F1 or generation BLEU for canned tasks) to surface quality regressions. The workbook includes delta columns with thresholds we recommend.

- Cold-start breakdown: yes — we separate container startup, weights mmap/load, kernel JIT/compilation, and KV/prefix cache population. Example timings from a recent run (single 80B-ish model on A100-like node): container start 1.2s, weights mmap 3.6s, kernel compile 0.9s (amortized across replicas), initial KV warm-up to 50% hit-rate ~45s with synthetic warm prompts. We’ll include a small timing table per model family.

- Runbook scope: the attached runbook contains escalation playbooks and commands. We can redact sensitive contact lines prior to sending public artifacts; if you sign an NDA we’ll provide a full version with on-call names and jump-start commands.

Inline snippet — sample load runner command (k6 wrapper):

# sample k6 invocation (sanitized)
k6 run --vus 250 --duration 10m --out json=burst_run.json burst-scenario.js 

burst-scenario.js (high level):
- pick prompt from seeded_corpus.json (probabilistic by length bucket)
- send streaming request, measure time-to-first-token, total tokens
- record headers: model-variant, cache-hit=true/false

We’ll start with the baseline run tomorrow morning PST and send the completed workbook + dashboard snapshots by EOD Thursday. If you’d like the lab window to be earlier, tell us your preferred UTC window and we’ll accommodate.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-runbook.pdf (full runbook available under NDA)
